articleTitle: A Novel Control System for Intelligent Nursing Robot
abstract: With the intensifying global issue of population aging, the number of disabled elderly individuals is increasing, leading to a significant rise in the demand for their daily care. Traditional caregiving methods require substantial human labor, imposing a heavy burden on the families of patients. Intelligent nursing robots can move flexibly indoors and perform various caregiving tasks, meeting the needs of disabled elderly individuals and alleviating the burden on caregivers. This paper proposes an intelligent nursing robot based on a Mecanum wheel mobile platform, which significantly reduces vibrations during navigation and obstacle avoidance through optimized motion control algorithms, thereby improving riding comfort. The robot is equipped with multiple caregiving functions, including navigation, toileting, and bed-chair docking. The control system employs an STM32F407 microcontroller, communicates with the upper computer via WIFI, and integrates PID and sliding mode control algorithms to achieve precise and smooth control of the drive motors. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized control algorithms significantly reduce the amplitude and frequency of vibrations, enhancing the riding comfort of the intelligent nursing robot. This provides an effective technical solution to the caregiving challenges faced by disabled elderly individuals.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Mobile Suspension Rehabilitation Robot
abstract: To address the growing issue of stroke rehabilitation, a mobile suspension rehabilitation robot is proposed. The design and functionality of the robot and each of its modules are elaborated in detail. Additionally, a kinematic model of the robot's chassis is established and its validity is confirmed through simulation. This forms a solid foundation for the future precise control of the chassis.

articleTitle: Upper Limb Rehabilitation Device Based on Adaptive Impedance Control
abstract: This article studies an upper limb rehabilitation device based on adaptive impedance control based on the different rehabilitation needs of stroke patients after surgery. First, under passive training, the device restores the patient's muscle strength by guiding the patient to perform periodic movements on a predetermined trajectory. Secondly, an impedance controller with joint driving torque as the control quantity is designed to provide moderate resistance by changing the damping coefficient. Strengthen the patient's muscle strength, and use fuzzy control algorithms to match individual impedance parameters based on the patient's maximum activity angle and maximum activity muscle strength. At the same time, virtual rehabilitation games are combined to motivate patients to train and enhance patients’ confidence in rehabilitation. Finally, experiments were conducted to test that the device can be combined with rehabilitation games for active and passive training, verifying its stability and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Development of a Novel and Cost-Effective Meal Assistance Robot for Self-Feeding
abstract: Over recent years, a variety of meal-assistance robots have been developed, aimed at enhancing the quality of life for individuals suffering from conditions such as Parkinson's disease and stroke. To counteract the prevalent limitations of currently available meal-assistance robots, including high cost, complex operation, and limited dietary options, we have pioneered the development of a new, cost-effective, integrated feeding robot. This robot embodies a simplistic design that features a turntable, a lifting module, a telescopic rotating module, and a combined bowl-spoon mechanism, thus enabling users to select their preferred dishes via an intuitive button interaction interface. Experimental findings demonstrated that our developed feeding robot could facilitate independent eating for patients, thereby not only reducing caregiver workload but also significantly upholding the personal dignity of patients.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multi-Posture Electric Wheelchair
abstract: In order to meet the needs of the elderly and the disabled for traveling and rehabilitation treatment, a multi-posture electric wheelchair with sitting, standing, lying and cushion tilting postures is designed. According to the functional requirements of daily care of the wheelchair, the design requirements of the multi-posture wheelchair are put forward, the design scheme of the wheelchair and the operation scheme of the mechanism are determined, and the feasibility of the mechanism is verified through kinematics calculation; the design of the structural scheme of the wheelchair is determined according to the results of the mechanism design and the correctness of the design is verified through ADAMS(Automatic Dynamic Analysis of Mechanical Systems). The physical prototype of the wheelchair is finally fabricated, and the results show that the wheelchair is smooth in movement, safe and reliable and it can realize the expected multiple posture adjustment modes.

articleTitle: Qt-Based Software System Design for Lower Limb Exoskeleton Safety Testing Platform
abstract: To achieve the visualization of the operational status data of the lower limb exoskeleton safety testing platform, an upper computer software based on the cross-platform Qt graphic library framework was designed in the object-oriented C++ programming language; the software decodes and analyses the received motion data, the main page implements functionalities including the display of motion parameter detection data, plantar pressure data, z-axis vertical center of mass displacement changes, and the final presentation of safety testing results. Firstly, the structure and principle of the self-designed lower limb exoskeleton safety test hardware platform and the software implementation process are introduced; then the functions of the upper computer software and the design and implementation process are introduced; finally, the lower limb exoskeleton safety test platform is used as an experimental object to validate the effectiveness of the designed upper computer software.

articleTitle: Design and Kinematic Research of a Multi-Interaction Integrated Rigid-Flexible Coupling Structure Meal Assistance Robot
abstract: The development and application of meal assistance robots are effective approaches to help elderly individuals with impaired hand function to independently feed themselves, particularly in the context of the exacerbated aging population and shortage of caregivers. In this paper, we present a multi-interaction integrated meal assistance robot designed to meet the needs of upper limb function-impaired patients for independent feeding. The robot features six degrees of freedom, with some joints employing flexible joint designs to provide inherent flexibility, resulting in a hybrid rigid-flexible mechanical arm. Subsequently, kinematic analysis of the robot was conducted using the D-H method, yielding the forward kinematic equations and 8 sets of inverse kinematics solutions for the six joint angles, which were validated.

articleTitle: A Pilot Study on the Introduction and Interaction Creation of Communication Robots in Care Facilities: A Comparison of China and Japan
abstract: Interpersonal relationships are believed to be the main cause of turnover in Japanese nursing care settings [1]. Although nursing care robots aimed at improving communication in nursing care environments are known, existing research has mainly focused on the interactions between robots and elderly people [2]–[7]. There is insufficient research on how interactions between users and caregivers facilitated by robots affect the surrounding environment. As cross-border nursing care scenarios increase [10] [16], more diverse communications are expected [11] [16]. In this pilot study, we install AI-equipped communication robots in nursing care facilities in Taiwan, China, and Japan, and analyze the process of on-site interactions using fieldwork and VC-IOE research methods [3] [4].

articleTitle: Efficacy and Safety Assessment of Custom 3D-Printed Cervical Pillows for the Treatment of Mechanical Cervical Spondylosis Based on Finite Element Analysis
abstract: Objective: This study aims to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the custom 3D printed cervical pillow for the treatment of mechanical cervical spondylosis using the finite element method. Methods: A finite element model of the cervical spine and pillow was constructed using CT and 3D scanning data. The study calculated changes in cervical spine stress and deformation in a supine position under three conditions: lying naturally, using a latex pillow, and using a 3D-printed pillow. Results: The use of custom 3D printed cervical pillow significantly improved cervical deformation, generating only an additional 5.09% stress on the cartilage, and improved physiological curvature by 18.12% on first use. Conclusion: The custom 3D printed cervical pillow, with its lightweight, breathable, and comfortable advantages, can safely and effectively treat mechanical cervical spondylosis.

articleTitle: Hand Landmark Detection Approach for the Personalized Soft Wearable Robotic Hand on Post-Stroke Hand Rehabilitation
abstract: We present an innovative approach for hand landmark detection using a personalized soft wearable robot hand, facilitating task-oriented training in stroke rehabilitation. Our paper introduces the Ring-reinforced Soft Actuator (RSA), accommodating different hand sizes and enabling flexion and extension movements. Individually controlled finger actuators assist stroke patients in various grasping tasks. We also propose an automated method for landmark detection and joint measurement, enabling efficient development of customfit wearable robot hands. Additionally, we developed a wireless task board for seamless interaction with the soft robotic hand and placement of training objects. Evaluation with four stroke subjects demonstrated significant improvements in upper limb functions (FMA), hand motor abilities (ARAT, BBT), and maximum grip/pinch strength after 20 sessions of task-oriented training. These improvements persisted for at least three months post-training, highlighting the system's potential to enhance stroke rehabilitation and promote hand motor recovery. The personalized design allows for frequent hand practice and easy integration into regular rehabilitation routines.

articleTitle: A Particle Swarm Optimal Control Method for a Direct‐Drive Electro‐Hydraulic Ankle‐Foot Prosthesis
abstract: Existing powered ankle-foot prostheses (PAFP)have relatively low power density ratios and poor performance in practical applications. Direct-drive electro-hydraulic technology features high power density, a closed structure, and small volume. This paper presents a PAFP system based on direct-drive electro-hydraulic technology. Instead of the common practice of oil replenishment through replenishment valves, the system installs accumulators on both sides of the hydraulic circuit. This design enables the recovery of energy and amplification of power, while reducing the complexity of the hydraulic system and manufacturing costs of the PAFP system. Based on the establishment of a simulation model for the position control system of a PAFP, control parameters were adjusted and optimized through a PID controller and a Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm, thus achieving precise reproduction of the input angle control commands. Simulation analysis of the prosthetic power verified that the designed PAFP exhibits enhanced performance in terms of energy output.

articleTitle: New Generation Wearable Ankle Rehabilitation Robot in Undergraduate Courses
abstract: In daily life, the ankle joint is the most vulnerable joint in the human body. Coupled with the current trend of agin g populations, the number of ankle injuries is continuously incre asing. While traditional manual rehabilitation therapy is effectiv e, the growing number of patients has burdened therapists, leadi ng to a gradual decline in rehabilitation efficiency. This has brou ght certain pressure to the field of rehabilitation medicine, as tra ditional rehabilitation methods can no longer meet the needs of patients. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel wearable ankle rehabilitation robot(WARR). The portable ankle rehabilitation robot, designed with a hybrid mechanism, can be applied in vari ous scenarios. With three degrees of freedom, it can accomplish compound ankle joint movements such as inversion/eversion(Inv /Eve), dorsiflexion/plantarflexion(DF/PF), and abduction/adduct ion(Abd/ Add). It can conduct training in active, passive, and tea ching modes. Additionally, therapists can control the rehabilitati on robot through an application to provide targeted ankle joint rehabilitation training for patients. The application obtains the angle and force of ankle joint movement from the robot's built-i n angle and force sensors, and real-time displays and records the m through a UI operation panel designed with Qt for rehabilitat ion effect assessment. This study is not only significant in the fiel d of rehabilitation medicine but has also been integrated into un dergraduate courses, aiding students in better understanding the design and application of rehabilitation robots. It has enhanced teaching effectiveness and improved students' practical skills.

articleTitle: Advancing Virtual Surgery with Hybrid Soft Tissue Simulation Models
abstract: This article introduces a novel approach to soft tissue simulation for medical training and surgical planning. By integrating precise finite element model parameters with efficient spring models, we have achieved simulations that maintain computational efficiency and accurate feedback force calculations. The introduction of position-based dynamic constraints enhances the stability of the model during simulation, addressing common challenges in real-time medical simulations. Our approach offers a promising solution for realistic and practical applications within virtual surgical platforms.

articleTitle: A Study on Finger Grasping Action Classification Based on Multimodal Fusion
abstract: The gradual increase in the number of stroke patients is due to the gradual aging of our population and unhealthy lifestyles. Due to limited medical resources, many patients cannot receive rehabilitation training in a timely and effective manner. This paper proposes to recognize hand movements based on myoelectric sensors and curvature sensors, utilizing radial basis function networks and convolutional neural to classify finger movements with good results. The application of multi-sensor fusion improves human-machine interaction, enhances the ability to perceive the environment, better realizes human-centered machine control, and improves the assistive ability of rehabilitation robots.

articleTitle: Cosine Similarity Graph Attention Networks for Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) has been a long-standing human disorder, especially prevalent in children who do not yet have good communication skills, and the prevention and diagnosis of ASD is challenging. This has resulted in a variety of neural networks to help doctors intelligently assist in prediction, and graph neural networks (GNNs) have been highly successful in this task. The construction of graph structures, an extremely important component of graph neural networks, varies in the way they are constructed and makes a difference in disease prediction performance. In this paper, the cosine similarity method is used to address the problem of non-uniform data metrics due to differences in acquisition conditions between subjects. In order to solve the problem of neuronal death, the most commonly used activation function is replaced by elu, which is used and a higher classification accuracy is obtained, and the residual strategy is used so that the model can better learn the linear transformation in the task and enhance the model expression ability. Methods for fusing different phenotypic information to encode edge features were compared, where the best performance was improved by 3.1% compared to classical graph neural networks. New perspectives are provided for multi-site data analysis, and disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Structural Design and Simulation of Multifunctional Nursing Wheelchair
abstract: In response to the prevalent societal issues of disabled individuals lacking independent mobility in their daily lives, a multifunctional nursing wheelchair has been designed to address these challenges. The device is not only suitable for confined indoor environments but also capable of assisting individuals with limited mobility in transitioning between standing, sitting, and lying positions. Additionally, it can facilitate patients in toileting activities. In order to solve the shortcomings of the traditional posture changing wheelchair in terms of comfort during posture transformation, a novel structure is proposed: a unique eccentric distance compensating posture frame to solve the physiological squeezing problem caused by the inconsistency between the human knee joint and the rotation axis of the wheelchair leg panel. Finally, Adams simulation and validation of the posture frame developed based on the above features are performed.

articleTitle: Characterization Analysis and Stiffness Estimation of Variable Stiffness Actuator for Elbow Exoskeleton
abstract: Exoskeleton actuator with variable stiffness will hold compliant characteristic, which is more ergonomic as well as a safe interaction between robot and human. Therefore, a variable stiffness actuator was proposed. It can change the structural configuration and preload to achieve variable stiffness. Meanwhile, it can be integrated into the elbow exoskeleton to meet the needs of miniaturization and lightweight. Then, the relationship between the FMG signal and the elbow joint stiffness of human-robot interaction was investigated. Machine learning methods were conducted to obtain a stiffness prediction model for real-time estimation. Finally, an elbow exoskeleton was developed. Furthermore, elbow flexion and extension trajectory tracking tests were carried out to evaluate the characterization of the elbow exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Developing a Robot-assisted in Situ Bioprinter Using Extrusion Technology
abstract: In situ bioprinting technology, a novel branch of traditional ex vivo bioprinting, directly deposits bio-ink onto a patient's defective area. This study introduces a UR5-assisted bioprinting system with six degrees of freedom to address issues such as tissue mismatch at the defect site, complex operations, and high costs from conventional bioprinting technologies. The system's end-effector integrates hardware and software on an STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller to control air pressure extrusion and bio-ink temperature. It featured a Peltier module and corresponding water-cooling block for temperature regulation, along with an external air compressor and proportional valve for precise extrusion control. The system's Graphical User Interface (GUI) incorporated a digital-twin model of the UR5 robotic arm, improving human-machine interaction and refining the planning of the printing path. The printing path programming converts G-code into JavaScript, executed by the UR5. Additionally, real-time monitoring of the printing path was displayed directly on the GUI. The overall in situ bioprinting system was validated by bioprinting Pluronic F127 into 2D images and a 3D scaffold on an actual femur model. The fidelity of the in situ bioprinting system was quantified by comparing the area error of printed results with preset images.

articleTitle: Effect of Haptic Perception Rehabilitation Robot Training on Hand Grasping Function After Stroke
abstract: Backgroud: The impaired hand function after stroke severely affected the patients' activities of daily living. Robot-assisted training is a supplementary method to promote the recovery of hand motor function, but few studies have reported the effect of haptic perception rehabilitation robots on hand grasping function after stroke. Objective: To investigate the effect of haptic perception rehabilitation robot training on the recovery of hand grasping function after stroke. Methods: This study was a single-blind randomized controlled trial. 44 stroke patients were randomly divided into experimental group (n = 22) and control group (n = 22). On the basis of conventional rehabilitation training, the experimental group received the grasp training session assisted by the haptic perception rehabilitation robot for 20 min, and the control group received the conventional hand grasp training session for 20 min. Grasp and grip part in action research arm test (ARAT), grip strength, modified Ashworth scale (MAS), total active movement (TAM) and Barthel index (BI) were used to evaluate the recovery of hand grasping function and activities of daily living before and 20 training sessions. Results: Compared with the therapist-assisted hand function training, the haptic perception rehabilitation robot training improved the grasping function and TAM of stroke patients (P < 0.05). However, there were no significant changes in other clinical outcome indicators (P > 0.05). Conclusion: The haptic perception rehabilitation robot training can help to restore the hand grasp function after stroke.

articleTitle: Design and Validation of an Inertial Motion Capture System for Human Dynamic Balance Assessment
abstract: The assessment of human balance ability holds significant clinical importance for enhancing health, preventing injuries, monitoring rehabilitation progress, and optimizing sports and physical training programs. This study introduced a system with 17 low-cost inertial measurement units (IMUs) to capture human motion data and analyze balance parameters, providing essential balance analysis for clinical patients. Initially, we utilized the inertial motion capture system to collect full-body motion IMU data and fed the data into OpenSim's human body model for calculating and analyzing gait kinematics. Subsequently, we calculated kinematic parameters relevant to human balance assessment based on human motion characteristics. To validate the feasibility of our approach, we recruited two subjects for walking experiments. We computed parameters related to human gait, posture control, and joint range of motion from the IMU data collected. These parameters were compared with those from an optical motion capture system, which was considered as the gold standard. The inertial motion capture system exhibited a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.027 m for stride length, 0.031 m for lateral swing position of the lower limb segment center of mass, 0.010 m for vertical swing position of the lower limb segment center of mass, 7.2° for knee joint flexion angles, and 5.1° for elbow joint flexion angles. The results indicate that the newly developed inertial motion capture system and method accurately estimated parameters related to dynamic balance, showing potential for practical applications and can be used as a reliable tool for gait analysis and balance assessment in various settings.

articleTitle: Exploration and Improvement: Survey and Recommendations on the Institute's Management System
abstract: This study systematically collected the views and suggestions of teachers and students on the management system of the institute by conducting a research on the management system of the institute, using questionnaires and expert interviews as the main methods. It is found that the current management system of the institute has some problems in terms of cumbersome processes, non-transparent information and inefficient implementation. In response to these problems, this paper proposes a series of improvement measures, including simplifying the process, strengthening information disclosure, and strengthening implementation. Finally, this paper puts forward hopes and prospects for the future development of the Institute and calls on all teachers and students to work together and contribute to the further development of the Institute.

articleTitle: A Clinical Pathway Model for Severe Stroke Rehabilitation based on Process Mining
abstract: Cerebral stroke, as a disease resulting from cerebral circulatory disorders, continues to have a stubbornly high incidence rate. With the ongoing advancements in rehabilitation technology, the number of rehabilitation programs concerning cerebral stroke is gradually increasing. However, there remains a deficiency in clinical pathways for the rehabilitation of severe stroke, resulting in an absence of unified standards to delineate the rehabilitation protocols and expected outcomes at each stage. Therefore, it is imperative to explore clinical pathways for the rehabilitation of severe stroke via advanced techniques. This study employs process mining techniques to analyze the rehabilitation process of severe stroke patients based on the collected patient data. Following data normalization and preprocessing, appropriate process mining algorithms are selected to establish clinical pathway models for severe stroke rehabilitation. Fuzzy models in process mining are utilized to explore the clinical processes associated with severe stroke patients through specific rehabilitation projects. From the output process model, it can be observed that the patient's rehabilitation process generally commences with cardiovascular and pulmonary physical therapy, as well as Neurophysical therapy. Multiple treatment methods are employed simultaneously, culminating in life-oriented occupational therapy. The entire rehabilitation process is adaptive, evolving with the patient's condition.

articleTitle: Constant Force Self-Tuning Control of Bathing Assistance Robots Based on GA-Fuzzy-PID Algorithm
abstract: This study addresses the issue of constant force control for a bathing assistance robot's end-effector during direct contact with human skin. A novel constant force control algorithm for the robot is proposed. Initially, based on establishing a contact model between the robot's end-effector cleaning tool and the skin, a GA-Fuzzy-PID controller was designed. Genetic algorithms were employed for iterative optimization to find appropriate PID parameters; subsequently, fuzzy control was utilized to adjust the PID coefficients in real-time. Finally, the control system was simulated using MATLAB/Simulink, comparing the effects of four control algorithms on the control of the constant force system during cleaning, and both constant and variable force tracking experiments were conducted. Simulation results demonstrated that compared to traditional PID, GA-PID and Fuzzy PID, the GA-Fuzzy-PID significantly improved the accuracy and robustness of constant force control, reducing peak error to 0.03 and decreasing overshoot by 41.97%, 42.09% and 10.74<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on the Design and Evaluation of Virtual Driving Simulator Product Based on KE-FAHP
abstract: The study intends to design virtual driving simulators that meet user expectations and market demands, aiming to enhance user experience and market competitiveness and better serve vehicle driving training. Differential needs of various user groups were explored through Kansei Engineering (KE), and design elements of virtual driving simulators were extracted based on lexical inference. An evaluation index model for design elements was constructed using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), with the weight of each index element being calculated. Subsequently, the design effectiveness of virtual driving simulators was scientifically assessed through the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) method, leading to the derivation of the optimal solution. Key factors influencing the design of virtual driving simulators include anthropometric compatibility, overall comfort, structural safety and stability, openness, ease of operation, and realism. Considering each element in a targeted manner during practical application can render the design and optimization process more efficient. The combination of KE and the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) validated the scientific nature of design research, providing effective references for subsequent product design endeavors.

articleTitle: Parallel Upper Limb Rehabilitation Robot and AnyBody Man-Machine Coupling Analysis
abstract: Neurorehabilitation robots are a crucial tool for facilitating rehabilitation training. This paper introduces a parallel upper limb neurorehabilitation robot designed for patients with upper limb motor disorders, providing efficient rehabilitation training. The robot is composed of a parallel five-bar mechanism, control motors, and an interactive screen, and includes both active and passive training functions. The Vicon motion capture system records the trajectory data of rehabilitation movements, which are used as the desired trajectories for passive training to ensure the effectiveness and appropriateness of the training movements. Additionally, the Vicon system, in conjunction with the AnyBody modeling software, is used to create a human-machine coupled model that simulates the patient's active training process. This model provides data on muscle changes during training, enabling a quantitative assessment of the movement process, which supports evaluations of the patient's rehabilitation status and motor capabilities.

articleTitle: Quantitative Assessment of Lower Limb Spasticity Using sEMG Data and Bayesian-Optimised SVM
abstract: Evaluation of lower limb spasticity plays a pivotal role in enhancing rehabilitation outcomes for stroke patients. Traditional assessment methods, such as Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), are prone to subjective biases, resulting in inconsistent evaluations among clinical practitioners. On the contrary, neurophysiological approaches, particularly the analysis of surface electromyography (sEMG) data, offer a more objective and sensitive alternative. While previous research has predominantly focused on upper limb spasticity, there exists a notable gap in the evaluation of lower limb spasticity. In this study, we introduce a Bayesian-optimized Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for the objective assessment of lower limb spasticity using sEMG data. The experiment involved seven participants at four MAS levels, and the results showed an average recognition accuracy exceeding 75% with optimal model and sEMG features. This innovative method holds promising potentials in the enhancement of objectivity and precision in lower limb spasticity assessment, effectively addressing the limitations associated with subjective biases in traditional evaluation approaches.

articleTitle: Advanced Techniques in Semiconductor Defect Detection and Classification: Overview of Current Technologies and Future Trends in AI/ML Integration
abstract: This review evaluates advancements and future trends in semiconductor defect detection methods, which are critical for enhancing electronic components' efficiency and reliability. As semiconductor devices shrink and become more complex, the accuracy of defect detection becomes crucial. This paper traces the evolution from manual inspections to the use of advanced technologies such as automated vision systems, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML). It discusses various defects like crystallographic errors, surface anomalies, and chemical impurities that affect device functionality and longevity, emphasizing the need for precise identification. The shift to ML and deep learning (DL) represents a significant move towards more adaptive, accurate, and faster detection methods. The paper outlines challenges like the miniature scale of modern devices, high costs of advanced imaging technologies, and the need speed in mass production. It identifies a critical gap between current technological capabilities and industry needs, particularly in scalability and processing throughput. Future research directions are suggested to close these gaps, including enhancing AI computational efficiency, developing new materials for better imaging contrast, and integrating these technologies seamlessly into production lines. This synthesis of current technologies and exploration of future trends aims to advance the dialogue and development of more effective defect detection and classification methods, leading to the production of more reliable semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Torque Bioinspired Knee Exoskeleton Based on the Gear Structure
abstract: This paper proposes a novel bioinspired knee joint structure characterized by high torque efficiency. After analyzing the experiment data of the knee joint, we found that there was the linear relationship between the angular variations induced by relative rolling and sliding in femur and tibia. Based on the conclusion, a compound motion of planetary gear mechanism and three-stage gear transmission mechanism is designed to simulate the motion characteristics of the knee joint in the sagittal plane. The high efficiency of the gears and the reduction ratio of approximately 6.8 allow this structure to be applied in scenarios requiring high torque when driven directly by a motor. Subsequently, the joint simulation between the human knee joint and the exoskeleton is constructed and executed using Simulink in MATLAB. Results indicate that during the flexion-extension process of the knee joint, the maximum displacement between the exoskeleton shank strap and the human body is 5mm, and the angular deviation is floating from -3 degree to +3 degree. Hence, the structure can follow the movement of knee and enhance wearable comfort of patients.

articleTitle: Design of Body-weight-support Training System Based on Center of Gravity Prediction
abstract: Facing the gait and balance rehabilitation training needs of patients with lower limb movement disorders, this paper, based on the principle of weight support walking rehabilitation and with the goal of realizing multifunctional weight reduction and real-time following of human body movement during dynamic movement, designs a weight support walking training system that is beneficial to help people with lower limb impairments to reduce the weight bearing of the lower limbs, improve the balance, and restore the basic walking ability. A multimode corrective control method based on the prediction of the center of gravity is proposed to address the problems of poor stability of weight reduction force and low precision of weight reduction in the dynamic training environment. The experimental results of rehabilitation training show that the designed walking training system has fast dynamic response, the steady state error of the dynamic support force of the lanyard is controlled within the range of ±5KG, and the multiple rehabilitation training modes can satisfy the safe rehabilitation training of patients at different stages, which proves the practicability of the designed control system and control strategy.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of MEMS-Based Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensors with COMSOL
abstract: We employ COMSOL Multiphysics to develop and analyze a novel tri-layered MEMS-based capacitive pressure sensor. The sensor comprises gold electrodes, a composite dielectric layer consisting of silver nanowires (AgNWs) embedded in thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), and a polydimethylsiloxane substrate. This study investigates the impact of variations in design parameters of the AgNW/TPU dielectric layer – specifically thickness and area – on sensor performance from 0 Pa to 15 kPa. The focus is on the sensor's response across different pressure levels, particularly at the maximum of 15 kPa. Preliminary simulation results indicate potential for performance enhancement. Future work will further optimize sensor sensitivity and accuracy by simulating additional three-dimensional dielectric layer configurations.

articleTitle: Development of a Soft Hand and Wrist Rehabilitation Robot Utilizing Lattice Structure Actuators
abstract: Soft robots offer promising solutions for rehabilitation due to their inherent attributes such as suppleness, lightweight construction, and safety features. However, prevalent soft actuators face limitations in output force and bending angle, impeding their effective application in rehabilitation. This paper proposes a novel design approach employing a two-layer lattice structure actuator, comprising flexion, guiding, and extension layers. This innovative design facilitates supple and efficient bi-directional rehabilitation training for fingers and wrists. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed dual-layer lattice structure actuator. At an air pressure of 150 kPa, it achieves an end force of 14.88 N, marking a remarkable 906% increase compared to its single-layer counterpart. Additionally, the dual-layer structure exhibits a minimum bending radius of 2.77 cm under 60 kPa, representing a 38.5% reduction relative to the single-layer actuator. Leveraging these actuators, a hand and wrist rehabilitation robot was developed and subjected to a clinical trial involving two healthy subjects. The trial outcomes reveal significant improvements in finger grasping ability and wrist range of motion with the assistance of the rehabilitation robot. These results underscore the practical usability and effectiveness of the soft hand and wrist rehabilitation robot, thereby holding promise for enhancing patient rehabilitation outcomes.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a 6-Degree-of-Freedom Parallel Ankle Rehabilitation Robot Based on Compliant Spherical Joints
abstract: The ankle joint is a crucial joint that supports walking in the human body. Ankle rehabilitation robots can effectively reduce the workload of caregivers and shorten the recovery time for patients. This paper proposes a 6-degree-of-freedom parallel ankle rehabilitation robot based on compliant spherical joints. First, a 6-degree-of-freedom parallel ankle rehabilitation robot based on compliant spherical joints is designed based on the Stewart platform configuration, and a kinematic analysis of the entire rehabilitation robot is conducted. Then, the compliant spherical joint is statically modeled using the matrix displacement method based on the nodal force balance equation, followed by a modal analysis. Finally, simulations of the 6-degree-of-freedom poses verify the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Exoskeleton-Based Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot Design and Simulation for Children with Cerebral Palsy
abstract: Squat gait is the most common abnormal gait in children with cerebral palsy. Gait training with lower limb rehabilitation robots can improve rehabilitation efficiency and reduce manual labor for them. A novel exoskeleton-based lower limb rehabilitation robot for children with cerebral palsy is proposed, considering the squat gait characteristics of children with cerebral palsy. The structure of the lower limb rehabilitation robot, which combines hip and knee with 4 active degrees of freedom exoskeleton and mobile walker, is designed and optimized. Static analysis of the key mechanical structure of the exoskeleton is conducted using ANSYS Workbench, and local structures are optimized to ensure the safety factor of the mechanical structure is greater than 1, guaranteeing reasonable structural strength and stiffness design. Dynamic simulation analysis based on the ADAMS model validates the reliability and dynamic walking effect of the lower limb exoskeleton rehabilitation robot, obtaining the curve relationship between joint angles and motion cycles, thus verifying the effectiveness of the mechanical system motion.

articleTitle: Robust Command-Filtered Control of Compliant Actuator-Driven Robotic Manipulators by Employing Beneficial Disturbances
abstract: A novel tracking control method is proposed for compliant actuator-driven robots in presence with parameter uncertainties, unknown nonlinear system dynamics, and external disturbances. The main feature of the proposed method is that beneficial parts of the lumped disturbances are retained to further improve tracking performance, rather than disturbances being fully seen as harmful elements to eliminate. Besides, its implementation requires only one system parameter, i.e., the motor inertia, which greatly eliminates the requirement for a priori knowledge of model parameters. Firstly, two extended state observers are designed to estimate unknown disturbances and unmeasurable system states. With the help of estimated information, disturbance effect indicators are constructed to evaluate whether the disturbance is beneficial or detrimental concerning current system motion. Then, a novel disturbance effect-triggered backstepping controller is proposed, in which the output tracking error of the system is guaranteed to converge into a small neighborhood of origin. In addition, it should be pointed out that the problem of “complexity explosion” is successfully avoided by introducing the filters into each step of the backstepping controller. Finally, the excellence of the recommended control method is validated by experiments.

articleTitle: Development of an EMG-controlled Hand Rehabilitation Exoskeleton with Series Elastic Actuators
abstract: With the improvement of living standards, the increased incidence of cardiovascular disease has led to an increased likelihood of stroke in elderly people, resulting in defects of hand function. In this paper, an underactuated hand rehabilitation exoskeleton is proposed to help them regain hand function. The exoskeleton uses a series elastic actuator (SEA) to achieve bidirectional flexible drive of the joint and uses electromyographic (EMG) signal control based on muscle force estimation. Structurally, to be able to rehabilitate three joints simultaneously and reduce the heavy weight of multiple motors, a single SEA with a linear motor was used for each finger. The three joints of the hand move through a multi-link coupling mechanism. At the same time, the SEA realizes force feedback without force sensors. Exoskeletons can also reduce discomfort caused by misaligned joints. In terms of control, EMG signals are used to achieve muscle force estimation, aiming to control exoskeleton movement. Then we conducted the SEA stiffness calibration experiment, muscle force estimation experiment and adjustment tests of different admittance parameters experiment.

articleTitle: Reforming the Undergraduate Curriculum of Biomedical Testing Technology: Challenges and Strategies
abstract: Biomedical testing technology plays a crucial role in modern medicine, encompassing disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis monitoring. With the rapid advancements in this field, higher education institutions face the challenge of updating their curricula to ensure graduates are well-prepared with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills. This study investigates the current issues in the undergraduate biomedical testing technology curriculum, such as outdated content, disconnect between theory and practice, insufficient multidisciplinary integration, and lack of student engagement. We propose a comprehensive reform strategy to address these challenges, including enhancing the balance between theory and practice, integrating cutting-edge knowledge, fostering multidisciplinary learning, and adopting innovative teaching methods. The goal is to improve the overall learning outcomes and competencies of students, equipping them with the skills needed to excel in their future careers and contribute to the advancement of biomedical testing technology.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design and Preliminary Experiment of an Orthopedic Rehabilitation Exoskeleton Based on the Coupled Movable Pulley Mechanism (CMPM)
abstract: During the bone tissue proliferative phase following fracture surgery, axial mechanical stimulation has been shown to facilitate bone healing. This study introduces the mechanism, conceptual design and preliminary experiment of an innovative lower limb orthopedic rehabilitation exoskeleton utilizing the Coupled Movable Pulley Mechanism (CMPM). Unlike conventional exoskeletons that merely offer assistive torque for knee movement, the effector of this exoskeleton additionally exerts controlled axial load at the femur or tibia fracture sites to provide tunable mechanical stimulation. This paper delves into the foundational principles of CMPM and design of the exoskeleton, develops a cable-driven force feedback control system for axial load exertion and knee joint support, and validates CMPM's anticipative functions by experiments. The results suggest that the proposed effectors play a dual role in post-fracture rehabilitation, i.e., providing axial loading stimulation and knee support. This research will potentially expedite post-surgical recovery in orthopedics, enhancing rehabilitation efficiency and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: A usability evaluation model for a bionic massage device: A bionic massage device based on the seated knee adjustment method as a validation
abstract: Bionic massage devices have been widely used in rehabilitation therapy settings, yet no systematic research exists for their usability evaluation. Therefore, this paper proposes a usability evaluation model for inic massage devices and uses a bionic massage device based on the seated knee adjustment manipulation as the evaluation object to demonstrate the feasibility of the model. The test results show that the bionic massage device meets the stiffness requirements and there are certain risk mitigation measures in terms of safety; in terms of effectiveness, the Pearson correlation coefficient between the bionic force output and the practitioners's massage force is 0.556 (p<0.01), which basically reproduces the practitioners's massage force, and the reachable range of the end massage head meets the human body size parameters; in terms of comfort, the comfort questionnaire found that the user is concerned about the comfort of the massage and the electromyography (EMG) data showed that users had perceived fatigue during the massage process. The test results show that the evaluation model can effectively evaluate the usability of the device and suggest human improvement solutions based on ergonomics.

articleTitle: Emotional Design of Elderly Companion Robot Based on KANO Model
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To cope with the accelerating trend of aging, relieve the pressure of social and family pension, meet the needs of the elderly population, and enrich the design and research of intelligent robot products for the elderly population. METHODS: (1) Review the development status of companion robots for the elderly by combing and analyzing relevant literature; (2) Combining the three-level model of emotional design with KJ method, qualitative analysis is made on the needs of the elderly group to obtain the elements of emotional design needs; (3) Using the Kano model to conduct quantitative evaluation and functional ranking of the emotional needs model, and design the product according to the evaluation results. RESULTS: According to the results of the emotional-KANO model assessment to modelling design of products, make the product model, check the appearance and the rationality of the structure and optimize the design. CONCLUSION: Under the guidance of this method, the emotional design of the elderly companion robot is feasible, which can quickly and accurately locate the needs of users, and provide a new path for the design innovation of assistive products for the elderly group.

articleTitle: A Multi-Wavelength Photoplethysmography-Based Patch Physiological Monitoring System: Design and Functional Validation
abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is a non-invasive optical technique that provides valuable physiological information, including heart rate (HR), pulse wave (PW), and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2). However, wearable devices often have variable signal quality, lacking monitoring capabilities or precision in daily use. To address these limitations, we propose a multi-wavelength PPG-based patch physiological monitoring system. The system utilizes three PPG wavelengths of enhanced signal quality, leading to improved accuracy and potentially extracting a wider range of physiological information compared to standard devices. We evaluated the system's performance by extracting PPG signals from three locations on the human body and analyzing their quality. The results demonstrate that the system successfully extracts high-quality PW, enabling accurate estimation of HR, SpO2, and even blood pressure (BP). The BP estimation model, particularly with personalized adaptation, exhibits good performance. The system offers the potential for continuous, non-invasive measurement of a wider range of physiological parameters compared to traditional wearable devices, and its portability and ease of use make it a compelling solution for user-friendly daily healthcare monitoring.

articleTitle: EMG Based Rehabilitation Gesture Recognition Using DAE-CNN-LSTM Hybrid Model
abstract: Stroke, as one of the leading causes of long-term disability globally, often results in motor impairments, particularly in the hands, significantly affecting patients' daily activities and causing profound psychological trauma. Rehabilitation gesture recognition, as one of the key means of active rehabilitation medicine, holds significant potential in stroke rehabilitation, providing real-time feedback on patient progress and enabling personalized interventions to meet individual needs. Traditional gesture recognition methods face numerous challenges when dealing with stroke patient data, such as noise, motion blur, and individual differences. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel approach for stroke patient gesture recognition using deep learning models. We adopt a strategy combining denoising autoencoder (DAE), convolutional neural network (CNN), and long short-term memory (LSTM) to enhance the accurate recognition of hand movements in stroke patients. Specifically, DAE is utilized for denoising EMG signals, extracting features, and reducing noise to improve the signal's noise resistance. CNN is employed for spatial feature extraction, while LSTM captures temporal dependencies in gesture sequences. By integrating these three deep learning models, our aim is to enhance the accuracy and robustness of rehabilitation gesture recognition. We validate the proposed method's effectiveness on an EMG dataset from seven subjects through experiments and compare it with traditional machine learning and individual CNN and LSTM algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements of our hybrid model in rehabilitation gesture recognition tasks, indicating promising application prospects and practical significance.

articleTitle: Adaptive Oscillator-Based Gait Event Detection and Trajectory Planning for Lower Limb Exoskeleton
abstract: Lower limb exoskeletons have been shown to have the potential to assist in patient rehabilitation and improve walking ability. How to accurately determine the patient's movement intention and plan an appropriate trajectory has been an important challenge in the control of lower limb exoskeletons. In this paper, we proposed a gait trajectory planning algorithm for lower limb exoskeleton based on adaptive oscillator and deep neural network to achieve continuous motion estimation of lower limb joints, which can adapt to changes in different walking speeds and maintain the desired trajectory. The proposed algorithm used real-time joint angle data to classify gait phases using neural network algorithms to determine gait characteristic event points. Then, we built an adaptive oscillator model to estimate the gait phases of the motion in real time and realize the online planning of the gait trajectory. A preliminary experimental study was conducted to validate the proposed online gait trajectory planning algorithm. The experimental results show that the online planning algorithm can adapt to different walking speed environments and obtain suitable desired trajectories for the exoskeleton.
